title: Pain Type and Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome Treatment
official: Mechanistic-Based Treatment of Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome
summary: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is a severe pain condition affecting 3-8 million people in the United States lacking treatments that work. Emotional suffering is common in IC/BPS and known to make physical symptoms worse, and studies show patient sub-groups respond differently to treatment. Individuals with IC/BPS have distinct subgroups, or "phenotypes," largely characterized by the distribution of pain throughout the body. Supported by our preliminary evidence, the overall goal of this project is to assess how IC/BPS phenotype may affect response to two different therapies often given without regard to patient phenotype, pelvic floor physical therapy (PT) and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) for IC/BPS.
conditions: Chronic Prostatitis With Chronic Pelvic Pain Syndrome
